h2: Explore every Container Office Cabin size and its plan
intro: Six approved general-arrangement plans, one controlled rate card. Pick the footprint by seat count, then check the door, window and partition line on the approved plan before you order.

panels.h3: 10x10 ft: the compact 100 sq.ft. cabin that seats four
panels.paragraph: One hundred square feet, one door and three windows. The approved plan puts four workstations around the walls with a clear centre, which is why this size works as a gate office, a store with a desk, or a two-shift supervisor cabin rather than a team room. At 10 ft square it drops onto a small levelled pad and lifts as one piece. It also carries the highest rate in the ladder, because a door, a distribution board and a roof do not get cheaper when the floor gets smaller.

Four workstations, four seats
One open room, no partition

Suits a gate office, a store with a desk, or a supervisor cabin

panels.h3: 20x8 ft: 160 sq.ft. of length for sites without width
panels.paragraph: Sixty per cent more floor than the 10x10 ft, and one seat fewer. That is not an error in the plan. Eight feet of internal width will not take facing desks with a working aisle, so the approved 20x8 ft runs a single three-station line down one wall under six windows. Choose it when the site gives you length but not width: a boundary wall, a service road edge, a strip between stacked material. If you need four seats or more, the 20x10 ft is the cheaper answer per seat.

Three workstations in a single line, three seats

panels.h3: 20x10 ft: the 200 sq.ft. reference size and base rate
panels.paragraph: Two hundred square feet is the reference configuration. The rate card, the calculator and the technical pack all start here, at Rs 1,250 per sq.ft. Ten feet of internal width is the point where facing desk runs and a usable aisle both fit, so the approved plan seats five where the 20x8 ft seats three at a similar cost. This is the size most site offices and small project offices settle on, and the one we hold closest to standard across both factories.

panels.h3: 30x10 ft: 300 sq.ft., twelve workstations, no partition
panels.paragraph: Three hundred square feet, two doors, eight windows and twelve workstations, with no internal partition. This is the open-plan size: one room, two entrances, desks along both long walls. The second door matters more than it sounds, because it lets you separate a site-facing entrance from a clean office entrance without building a wall and losing floor. If you would rather have a closed manager room than the extra open floor, step up to a 40 ft size.

panels.h3: 40x8 ft: a manager room on a narrow 320 sq.ft. plan
panels.paragraph: Three hundred and twenty square feet in a 40 ft long, 8 ft wide body, and the narrowest plan that still gives you a private room. The approved arrangement is a ten-foot manager cabin plus a thirty-foot common office, with three doors, ten windows, seven workstations and ten seats in total. The width still allows only one desk line in the common office. Pick it when the site is a long narrow strip and a closed manager room is not negotiable.

panels.h3: 40x10 ft: 400 sq.ft. and fifteen seats, manager included
panels.paragraph: Four hundred square feet, twelve workstations and fifteen seats, arranged as a ten-foot manager cabin and a thirty-foot common office with facing desk runs. It is the largest single module in this ladder and it carries the lowest rate per square foot. Check access before you choose it: a 40 ft body needs trailer approach, turning room and a clear crane position at both lift points. Where access is tight, two 20 ft cabins placed side by side often land more easily.
